## संशोधित final hypothesis (दो परिभाषात्मक सुधार सहित)

**Change-log:**
1. **"~38% of house size's loading variance on PC2" clause हटाई; स्थान पर दो सुपरिभाषित मात्राएँ (loadings_main.csv से पुनः-गणित):** (a) Zhausgr का PC2-per-PC2-उदायगार = loading² = 0.364² = **0.133, अर्थात PC2 (unit-norm loading vector) का ≈13%** — daggers 0.014 (≈1.4%) और hatchets/swords 0.004 (≈0.4%) के विरोधाभास में; (b) PC1–PC2 तल में Zhausgr की loading-vector की वर्ग-लंबाई का **72% (0.364²/0.430²) PC2 पर** है। मूल "38%" PC2²/Σ(loading² over PC1–PC4) था — तकनीकी रूप से पुनरुत्पादनीय पर अविवक्षित, अतः हटाया।
2. **"weapons" को top-driver सूची से हटाया।** PC1 के top drivers अब केवल: ZCU_AU (+0.399, rank 1), Zkeverz (+0.381, 2), ZKeform (−0.355, 3), ZHort (+0.343, 4) — यानि copper/gold, pottery decoration, pottery form (ऋणात्मक दिशा), और hoards/depots। Hatchets/swords (+0.301, rank 5) और daggers (+0.279, 6) को निरंतर **mid-rank covarying components** कहा जाएगा, जो स्वयं की "not its core drivers" रिपोर्ट से संगत है।

**अवशिष्ट सब कुछ अपरिवर्तित** (main run n=39, sign convention sum-of-loadings>0, EVR 31.8%/20.4%, biplot कोण 11°/35–45°, sensitivity runs)।

**payload.hypothesis (संशोधित):** In the PCA of the twelve capital forms analyzed in hundred-year time slices (n=39 slices, BCE 4300–500; PC1 explains 31.8% and PC2 20.4% of variance), the symbolic-capital components — house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) — all carry positive but mid-to-low-rank loadings on PC1 (+0.23, +0.28, +0.30; ranks 10, 6, 5 of 12): they increase together with a general capital-intensity axis whose top drivers are copper/gold, pottery decoration, pottery form (opposite-signed) and hoards/depots, with the two weapon variables themselves only mid-rank covarying components, and they reach their highest slice scores in the OBA/YBA (BCE 1400–1100); they thus covary with, but do not define, PC1. On PC2 they are distributed unevenly: house size is a substantive PC2 element — its squared PC2 loading (0.364² ≈ 0.13) accounts for roughly 13% of the unit-norm PC2 loading vector (versus ~1.4% for daggers and ~0.4% for hatchets/swords), and 72% of house size's squared loading length in the PC1–PC2 plane lies on PC2 — with its high values concentrated in positive PC2 scores of the Middle Neolithic/Funnel Beaker house-size peak (BCE 3500–3100); daggers (+0.12) and hatchets/swords (+0.07) are essentially neutral on PC2 and almost entirely PC1 phenomena. Consequently, in the PC1–PC2 biplot the two weapon variables are nearly collinear (11° apart) along positive PC1 while house size diverges from them by 35–45°, and the full symbolic-capital package (all three elevated) occurs only at BCE 1900–1800 (LN) and BCE 1400–1300 (OBA).

payload.workflow: Parsed capital.csv with decimal-comma convention (39 100-year slices, 12 pre-z-scored variables, 0 missing; 37/39 rows cross-verified against time_series_data.csv raw points); PCA via centered-matrix numpy SVD (sklearn-equivalent) without re-standardization; PC signs fixed so loadings-sum>0; extracted loadings/EVR/per-slice scores, trio variable–PC correlations, PC2 extremes by period, biplot loading angles; sensitivities: n=37 (PC1 stable, max|Δ|=0.099), drop-ZSichel (PC1 loading corr 1.000), re-standardized (corr 0.995). Final revision: replaced ambiguous '~38% PC2 share' with precisely defined quantities recomputed from loadings_main.csv (PC2 squared-loading share 13.3%; 72% of PC1–PC2-plane squared length on PC2), and removed 'weapons' from the PC1 top-driver list, retaining them as mid-rank covarying components. Pollen file context-only.
